title: Recipes
description: 171 ready-made training recipes spanning text (Llama 3.1/3.2/4, Qwen 2.5/3, the 2026 families Qwen 3.5/3.6, DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.1, Kimi K2.5/K2.6, MiniMax M3, plus QwQ-32B, Gemma 3, Phi-4, DeepSeek R1/V3, GPT-OSS, GLM 4.6, Granite 4), vision (Llama-3.2-Vision, Pixtral, Qwen2-VL, InternVL 3.5, LLaVA-Next, MiniCPM-V, Qwen-Image, DeepSeek-OCR, Paddle-OCR-VL), audio (Qwen2-Audio, Whisper, Voxtral, SeamlessM4T), ASR fine-tuning (whisper-tiny/base/large-v3, v0.71.32), TTS (Orpheus, Llasa, Oute), reasoning (DeepSeek-R1-Distill, Qwen3-Coder), edge (SmolLM2, Phi-3.5-mini, LFM2), domain specialists (BioMistral, Meditron, Mathstral, Magicoder, MedGemma, EmbeddingGemma), RAG (raft-llama3-8b, ra-dit-retriever, ra-dit-llama3-8b).

blocks.html:
Recipes

Soup includes 171 ready-made configs for popular models — v0.31 grew the catalog to 80, v0.51 added 26 new families (GPT-OSS / GLM 4.6 / Kimi K2 / MiniMax M2 / QwQ-32B / QVQ-72B / Granite 4 / Voxtral / DeepSeek-OCR and more), v0.52 added 6 TTS / BitNet recipes (Orpheus / Sesame-CSM / Llasa / Spark / Oute / Falcon-E; the Sesame-CSM, Spark and Falcon-E recipes were removed in v0.76.0), v0.62 added 3 RAG recipes (raft-llama3-8b, ra-dit-retriever, ra-dit-llama3-8b), v0.71.24 added 17 SFT recipes for the open-weight models released February to June 2026 (Qwen 3.5 / Qwen 3.6 / DeepSeek-V4 / GLM-5.1 / Kimi K2.5 / Kimi K2.6 / MiniMax M3; one of the 17 was removed in v0.76.0, see "Removed in v0.76.0" below), v0.71.26 added qwen2.5-coder-7b-sft (catalog 133 → 134), v0.71.30 added 3 GRPO rollout-env recipes (grpo-env-calculator, grpo-env-retrieval-qa, grpo-env-guess-number, catalog 134 → 137), v0.71.31 added online-dpo-smollm2-135m (catalog 137 → 138), and v0.71.32 added the ASR recipes whisper-tiny-asr / whisper-base-asr / whisper-large-v3-asr plus smolvlm-256m-sft (catalog 138 → 142), v0.73.3 added qwen3.5-4b-pretrain and deepseek-v4-flash-grpo (catalog 142 → 144), and v0.74.0 added nineteen more across the Qwen2.5-Coder and Qwen2.5-Math sizes, the DeepSeek-R1-Distill families in SFT and DPO, SmolLM3, and GRPO and DPO variants for the 2026 MoE giants (catalog 144 → 163), and v0.75.0 added four more, two DPO shapes for bases that already shipped SFT and GRPO plus two small Qwen3.5 GRPO recipes a contributor could actually run a few steps of (catalog 163 → 167), and v0.76.0 added nine and removed six (catalog 167 → 170): DPO and GRPO variants for DeepSeek-V4 Pro, Kimi K2.5, Qwen3.6 27B and Qwen3.6 35B-A3B, plus qwen3.5-35b-a3b-grpo, against the removal of six recipes that could not run (see "Removed in v0.76.0" below). Thirty-eight existing recipes were edited as well, some in more than one way: seven base model IDs were corrected, nine parameter-count labels were corrected, and 23 recipes now set lora.dropout: 0 (22 MoE recipes that keep moe_lora, where peft refuses dropout on fused expert parameters, and minimax-m3-sft, which kept the line when it dropped moe_lora). Three more (oute-tts, llasa-tts and online-dpo-smollm2-135m) were edited in other ways. v0.77.0 added qwen3.5-4b-dpo and qwen3.5-2b-dpo and removed pixtral-dpo (catalog 170 → 171), marked kimi-k2-sft and kimi-k2-thinking-grpo unavailable, and added training.gradient_checkpointing: true to 22 recipes (see below). No need to write YAML from scratch.

List Recipes

Shows all available recipes with model name, task, and description.

Search Recipes

blocks.code:
# Search by model name
soup recipes search llama

# Search by task type
soup recipes search grpo

# Search by model size
soup recipes search 8b

# Print full YAML to stdout
soup recipes show llama3.1-8b-sft

# Copy recipe to soup.yaml
soup recipes use llama3.1-8b-sft

# Custom output path
soup recipes use qwen2.5-7b-dpo --output my-config.yaml

Each recipe ships with LoRA rank, learning rate, batch size, and quantization tuned to the model. Use soup recipes show <name> to print the full YAML. A recipe that loads through the config schema is not necessarily one that runs, and the giant MoE recipes in particular are not trained by anyone here; read Before you run one first.

Gradient checkpointing in the RL and preference recipes (v0.77.0). Since v0.77.0 training.gradient_checkpointing reaches the TRL trainers, and with its default false the grpo, ipo, bco, reward_model and online_dpo tasks train with checkpointing off, where TRL's own default (on) used to apply. Every bundled grpo, ipo, reward_model and online_dpo recipe sets gradient_checkpointing: true at v0.77.0 (22 of them gained the line in this release), so a config written by soup recipes use keeps the memory it had. A config you wrote yourself from an older recipe needs the same line; see Speed & Memory.

"Native vision" in the Qwen 3.5 row describes the base model, not the recipes. Every Qwen 3.5, 3.6 and 3.8 recipe sets modality: text, so they load the language model alone through AutoModelForCausalLM, without the vision tower. They train the text model only and are not multimodal fine-tunes.

Unavailable since v0.77.0: the two Kimi K2 recipes

kimi-k2-sft (moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Base) and kimi-k2-thinking-grpo (moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Thinking) stay in the catalog but are marked unavailable, because a resident Kimi K2 load is refused at config load on Transformers 5.x (#2104, #2130). soup recipes show still prints their YAML (exit 0), and soup recipes list shows them with size N/A. soup recipes use prints the reason, writes nothing and exits 3:

  • kimi-k2-sft: Resident Kimi K2 is unsupported on Transformers 5.x. Use the guarded training.stream_layers: true route (#2107), with --trust-remote-code for the tokenizer and pip install tiktoken. ... Kimi-K2-Base and -Instruct are admitted only under layer streaming; upstream verified that route on CPU with a tiny K2-shaped checkpoint only, and nothing has been trained on K2 (see Streaming a Mixture-of-Experts base).
  • kimi-k2-thinking-grpo: Resident Kimi K2 is unsupported on Transformers 5.x. No supported route yet. Kimi-K2-Thinking has no supported route.

An unknown recipe name is still exit 1.

Check a recipe before you download it

blocks.code:
soup recipes verify                          # every shipped recipe, and the templates
soup recipes verify --no-templates           # recipes only
soup recipes verify --config soup.yaml       # one config of your own
soup recipes verify --json

blocks.html:
soup recipes verify answers one question for each config: can the LoRA adapter this config asks for attach to this base model? It builds the base's architecture on the meta device from its config.json alone (cut down to a few layers, which is enough for the module names to repeat), then runs Soup's own target resolution and the real peft attach, using the model class that config's trainer would load. No weights are downloaded and no remote code is run, but config.json for each base is fetched from the Hub, so catalogue mode makes one request per config and needs network access (set HF_TOKEN to check a gated repo). It needs the training stack (pip install "soup-cli[train]"); without torch, transformers and peft it exits 1 and names the fix.

Each config gets one of four verdicts:

VerdictMeaning
attachesThe adapter attached. The summary counts these and, if any adapted expert modules or a vision tower, says so
cannot_attachTarget resolution or the peft attach failed. The table names the stage (resolve, build or attach) and the reason
no_adapterThere is no adapter to attach: lora.r: 0 (full fine-tuning), backend: mlx (which attaches through a different path), a task whose trainer never builds one, or classifier_lora / asr_lora left off
unverifiedThe check could not be made here: a gated repo (set HF_TOKEN), a base that needs trust_remote_code, a config this transformers cannot read, or a config.json that could not be fetched. It is reported and never counted as a failure

Exit codes: 0 when everything that could be checked attaches, 2 when any config cannot attach, 3 for a missing or unparseable --config (since v0.76.1 that includes one larger than 1 MiB, or nested or expanding past the YAML limits; read from the code, not run; since v0.77.0 also a config refused at load, such as one that sets a staged field away from its default: Config does not parse: ... refused as of v0.77. Delete the line., run) or a mistyped option, 1 for a crash or a missing or broken torch, transformers or peft. --json prints one row per config with name, base, task, verdict, model_type, adapted, expert_modules, vision_modules and detail.

Exit 0 can mean nothing was checked. unverified never changes the exit code, and a config whose config.json cannot be fetched is unverified, so on a machine with no network (or HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1) the command can print 0 attach, 0 cannot, N have no adapter, M unverified. and exit 0. A CI job should read the summary line or the --json verdicts, not only the exit code. A config that attaches here has loaded its adapter; it does not mean the recipe trains, or that its base fits your card.

soup recipes verify was checked here only as far as its refusals: the help text, the exit-1 message when torch is missing, and the exit 3 for an unknown option were run. The verdicts and the offline behaviour above are read from the v0.76.0 code (commands/recipes.py and utils/attach_preflight.py; attach_preflight.py is unchanged at v0.77.0), not run, because the check needs torch.

Customizing Recipes

Recipes are a starting point. After soup recipes use, edit the generated soup.yaml to:

  • Point to your dataset (data.train)
  • Adjust epochs, learning rate, or LoRA rank
  • Add backend: unsloth for 2-5x speedup
  • Enable evaluation with eval config section
